challenge.method: Checked the cover, copyright page, chapter opening and neighboring object-model discussion. Compared the exact edge direction and target with the index identities and looked for language in the cited discussion that would justify applying the classification to a particular Pascal standard revision, a different supplier, or a later Delphi edition.
challenge.results: The cited sentence names the Delphi language as the extension and standard Pascal as the base. The following examples illustrate Delphi classes and objects. The cited passage supplies neither an ISO revision nor a conformance statement, and the publication establishes the 2002 Borland Delphi 7 for Windows scope.

limitations: The source establishes the dialect classification for Borland’s Delphi 7 language. Later Delphi editions and other Object Pascal traditions require their own evidence.
Standard Pascal is the base language named in this passage. Determining ISO/IEC 7185 conformance or selecting a standard revision requires separate evidence.
